description: Feature B — the pre-drive permission dialog backstop. When the user taps Start drive and permission is NOT 'granted', show a dialog FIRST explaining the drive needs location, with an 'Allow' button that triggers the native prompt (state 'prompt') or device-specific re-enable steps (state 'denied'). It is prompt-and-explain, never a hard gate: after the user responds (Allow or dismiss), the existing drive-start flow continues (vehicle picker when applicable, then drive; simulator ▶ fallback still works). When permission is already 'granted', Start drive proceeds straight into the normal flow with NO extra dialog. The dialog mirrors #vehicle-dialog's markup and a11y pattern. Depends on FEAT-001 (KPR.geoPermission, KPR.map.requestLocation). Cooperates with FEAT-002 via the shared permission state so granting through the strip means the dialog never appears.
steps:
In index.html, near the other dialogs at the end of (after #vehicle-dialog / #send-dialog), add:

Turn on location for this drive

. Mirror #vehicle-dialog exactly for structure/classes.

Create js/geo-dialog.js as an IIFE KPR.geoDialog mirroring evaluation.js's dialog helpers (openVehicleDialog/_closeDialog/_startFromDialog/_trapTab/_wireDialog). Keep internal dialogState ({ onDone, lastFocus }).

Implement open(onDone): if already open, return (no-op). Read KPR.geoPermission.getState(). Fill #geo-dialog-body via textContent: for 'prompt' -> 'This drive follows your location on the route. Tap Allow to turn it on.'; for 'denied' -> device-specific steps using KPR.geoPermission.isIOS() ('Location is blocked. Turn it on in Settings › Privacy › Location Services › Safari Websites, then reload.' on iOS, else 'Location is blocked. Allow it for this site in your browser's site settings, then reload.'). In 'denied', hide or relabel #geo-dialog-allow (e.g. hide it, since a denied geolocation cannot be re-prompted) so the only action is dismiss. Store onDone and lastFocus (document.activeElement), remove 'hidden' from #geo-dialog, and focus the primary actionable button.

Implement _close(): add 'hidden' to #geo-dialog, restore lastFocus, clear dialogState. Implement an Allow handler: in 'prompt' call KPR.map.requestLocation() then _close() and invoke onDone(); in 'denied' (if Allow is somehow active) just _close()+onDone(). Implement a dismiss handler (Not now) and Escape/backdrop-click that _close() and ALWAYS invoke onDone() — the dialog never blocks the drive.

Implement isOpen() and a Tab trap (_trapTab over the dialog's buttons) matching evaluation.js _trapTab. Wire all listeners in init() once (click on allow/dismiss, backdrop click on #geo-dialog, keydown for Escape + Tab). Return { init, open, isOpen }.

In js/drive.js start(): keep the existing guards (if active return; if !canStart() alert+return; if KPR.results.isActive() return). Then insert the permission gate BEFORE the vehicle-list branch: if KPR.geoPermission.getState() !== 'granted' && !KPR.geoDialog.isOpen() { KPR.geoDialog.open(() => _continueStart()); return; }. Extract the EXISTING body of start() (the vehicles = KPR.evaluation.getVehicles(); if (vehicles.length >= 1) { openVehicleDialog… } else { _begin({}); } block) verbatim into a new private function _continueStart(). When state IS 'granted', start() falls through and calls _continueStart() directly. This leaves the vehicle-picker path and the _begin/simulator flow unchanged.
Add <script src="js/geo-dialog.js"></script> to index.html AFTER js/drive.js, and call KPR.geoDialog.init() from the same app startup path as the other module init()s.

In tests/run.html: add the #geo-dialog fixture DOM block (matching the real ids/classes) and <script src="../js/geo-dialog.js"></script> to the script list. Do NOT add drive.js (it needs Mapbox) — the start()-integration is covered by manual verification; unit tests cover KPR.geoDialog directly.

Extend tests/enable-location.test.js (or add a geo-dialog section to it) to cover KPR.geoDialog using the FEAT-001 seam + a KPR.map.requestLocation spy: open() fills #geo-dialog-body per state (prompt vs denied, iOS vs generic text); Allow in 'prompt' calls the requester spy then invokes onDone; Dismiss and Escape invoke onDone WITHOUT calling the requester; in 'denied' the Allow button is hidden/inactive and dismiss still invokes onDone; open() while already open is a no-op (onDone from the first open not double-invoked).
acceptance_criteria: index.html contains #geo-dialog mirroring the #vehicle-dialog pattern (role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby, h3 title, .hint body, .button-row with secondary + primary buttons).
KPR.geoDialog.open(onDone) fills the body per permission state (prompt vs denied, iOS vs generic), and ALWAYS invokes onDone after the user responds (Allow, Not now, Escape, or backdrop).
Allow calls KPR.map.requestLocation() only in 'prompt'; in 'denied' there is no re-prompt (Allow hidden/inactive).

drive.js start() shows #geo-dialog first only when state is not 'granted'; when 'granted' it goes straight into _continueStart() (the unchanged vehicle-picker / _begin path). The simulator ▶ fallback remains reachable because the dialog never blocks _begin.
Running the test command ends with RESULT: PASS and a total count greater than the post-FEAT-002 count, with the geo-dialog assertions listed as ok.
verification: Run: powershell -NoProfile -File tests\run-tests.ps1 — confirm 'RESULT: PASS (N tests)' with N greater than the FEAT-002 total and the geo-dialog tests showing 'ok'.

Manual (served page, http://localhost:8000 with a token, a real route from samples/): with permission 'granted' Start drive shows NO extra dialog and goes straight to the normal flow; with 'prompt' it shows #geo-dialog, Allow triggers the native popup, then the vehicle picker (if any) and drive proceed; with 'denied' it shows the device-specific steps, no re-prompt, and dismissing still lets the drive start with ▶ simulate working. Confirm granting via the FEAT-002 strip first means Start drive shows no dialog.
findings: DONE. Suite: RESULT: PASS (336 tests), up from the post-FEAT-002 total of 327 (9 new geo-dialog tests, all 'ok'; render-audit DOM-safety suite still green). Module built — KPR.geoDialog (js/geo-dialog.js, IIFE, Mapbox-free), mirrors evaluation.js's #vehicle-dialog helpers: init() -> wires the dialog listeners once (idempotent via an internal `wired` flag; open() also calls _wire() so it is safe even if init() hasn't run). Wired in js/app.js init() immediately BEFORE KPR.drive.init(). open(onDone) -> no-op if already open (first onDone is NOT replaced). Reads KPR.geoPermission.getState(): in 'prompt' fills #geo-dialog-body (textContent) with 'This drive follows your location on the route. Tap Allow to turn it on.' and shows #geo-dialog-allow; in 'denied' fills device-specific steps (KPR.geoPermission.isIOS() -> 'Location is blocked. Turn it on in Settings \u203A Privacy \u203A Location Services \u203A Safari Websites, then reload.' else '...Allow it for this site in your browser's site settings, then reload.') and HIDES #geo-dialog-allow (a denied geolocation cannot be re-prompted). Stores { onDone, lastFocus: document.activeElement }, removes 'hidden' from #geo-dialog, and focuses the primary actionable button (Allow when visible, else the dismiss button). isOpen() -> dialogState !== null. _close() (private) adds 'hidden', restores lastFocus, clears dialogState BEFORE invoking onDone (so a re-entrant start() sees the dialog closed), and ALWAYS runs onDone once. Allow handler: in 'prompt' calls KPR.map.requestLocation() (guarded by a typeof check) then _close(); in 'denied' just _close(). Dismiss ('Not now'), Escape and a backdrop click all _close() and therefore always continue the drive. _trapTab cycles over the dialog's visible, enabled and . loaded immediately AFTER js/drive.js and before js/enable-location-strip.js. No new CSS was needed — it reuses the existing .dialog/.dialog-box/.hint/.button-row/.secondary-btn/.primary-btn styles. drive.js start() integration: the existing guards (if active return; if !canStart() alert+return; if KPR.results.isActive() return) are unchanged. After them a permission gate was inserted: if KPR.geoPermission && getState() !== 'granted' && KPR.geoDialog && !KPR.geoDialog.isOpen() { KPR.geoDialog.open(() => _continueStart()); return; } else start() falls through to _continueStart(). The ENTIRE original body of start() (the vehicles = KPR.evaluation.getVehicles(); vehicle-list branch -> openVehicleDialog, else _begin({})) was moved VERBATIM into a new private function _continueStart(). So when granted, start() -> _continueStart() with zero behavior change; when not granted, the dialog shows first and _continueStart() runs from its onDone after the user responds. The vehicle-picker and _begin/simulator paths are untouched, so the ▶ simulate fallback stays reachable (the dialog never blocks _begin). Startup wiring (js/app.js): KPR.geoDialog.init() is called in KPR.app.init() just before KPR.drive.init() (and before KPR.enableLocationStrip.init()). Tests: the geo-dialog assertions were ADDED to tests/enable-location.test.js as a second IIFE section (not a new file). It calls D.init() once then drives KPR.geoDialog directly, stubbing seams with the same helpers as the strip tests (withGeo swaps KPR.geoPermission.getState/isIOS; withMapSpy swaps KPR.map with { requestLocation: spy }), each restored in a finally; a closeIfOpen() helper dismisses any open dialog between tests. The 9 tests cover: open() in prompt shows the dialog with Allow-mentioning body and a visible Allow button; open() in denied (iOS) shows Safari steps and HIDES Allow; open() in denied (non-iOS) shows generic site-settings steps and hides Allow; body is textContent-only (no child elements); Allow in prompt calls the requestLocation spy once, closes, and invokes onDone; 'Not now' in prompt invokes onDone WITHOUT calling the spy; Escape invokes onDone WITHOUT calling the spy; dismiss in denied invokes onDone and never re-prompts; open() while already open is a no-op (first onDone registered once, second never registered). tests/run.html got the #geo-dialog fixture block (same ids/classes as index.html, inside #fixture-dom near #vehicle-dialog) and after start-chooser.js and before enable-location-strip.js. drive.js was NOT added to the harness (needs Mapbox) per the task; the start()-integration is covered by manual verification. Manual verification (per FEAT-003.json) was NOT run here (requires a served page with a Mapbox token and a real route); the unit suite covers KPR.geoDialog directly. Committed locally on branch location-permission-ui; not pushed.
